tagline: A Mekong-side city in Thailand's far east — Pha Taem, Sam Phan Bok, and the Candle Festival
introHtml: Ubon Ratchathani is a large province in lower Isan that sits on the Mekong at Thailand's far eastern edge — the spot where the sun rises first in the country, up at Pha Chanadai. Mention Ubon and most people picture Pha Taem, the cliff face covered in ancient rock paintings above the river; Sam Phan Bok, the rocky rapids in the middle of the Mekong that surface in the dry season; and the Candle Festival every July, when temples carve wax into intricate floats. In town there are old temples, markets, and food with a clear Vietnamese influence. If you like a trip that mixes Mekong-side nature with local culture, Ubon keeps you busy for several days without getting dull.
bestTime: November–February for cool, easy weather. Sam Phan Bok is at its best in the dry season, roughly January–May, and the Candle Festival falls in mid-July.

highlights.name: Pha Taem National Park
highlights.blurb: A cliff above the Mekong with prehistoric rock paintings thousands of years old, plus wide-open views across the river to Laos.

highlights.name: Sam Phan Bok
highlights.blurb: Rocky rapids in the middle of the Mekong that emerge in the dry season, revealing thousands of eroded basins often called the Grand Canyon of the Mekong. Easy to spend the whole day walking and shooting photos.

highlights.name: Candle Festival
highlights.blurb: The city's signature event in mid-July, when intricately carved wax candles from different temples are paraded around town. People come from all over the country to see it.

highlights.name: Pha Chanadai
highlights.blurb: The first spot in Thailand to see the sunrise, within the Pha Taem area. Get up before dawn and wait for the first light over the Mekong.

highlights.name: Wat Thung Si Muang and Thung Si Muang Park
highlights.blurb: An old temple in the city center with a beautiful scripture hall standing over water, next to Thung Si Muang Park — the ground used for the Candle Festival and a favorite spot for locals to relax.

highlights.name: Wat Sirindhorn Wararam Phu Prao (the Glowing Temple)
highlights.blurb: A hillside temple in Sirindhorn district with a wishing tree that glows green behind the ordination hall after dark. People flock here to see it.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, larb, koi, grilled chicken, and bamboo-shoot soup — bold flavors you'll find all over town, and the everyday staples for locals here.

foodScene.name: Pho and Vietnamese food
foodScene.note: Ubon has had a Vietnamese-descended community for generations, so pho, nem nuang (grilled pork rolls), fresh spring rolls, and khao piak noodles turn up at many spots in town.

foodScene.name: Moo yor and Chinese sausage
foodScene.note: Well-known souvenirs with a Vietnamese influence. Moo yor is a firm pork sausage eaten with sticky rice, and people buy it by the bundle to take home.

foodScene.name: Kuay jab yuan
foodScene.note: Vietnamese-style kuay jab noodles in a clear broth, topped with pork and fried garlic. A breakfast dish locals in Ubon eat regularly.

foodScene.name: Fresh khanom jeen with curry sauce
foodScene.note: House-made khanom jeen noodles topped with a rich curry sauce, eaten with a big pile of local vegetables. Easy to find at the morning markets.

foodScene.name: Khao jee and sticky rice
foodScene.note: Grilled sticky rice brushed with egg, a morning snack. A local staple that's easy to grab at roadside stalls and markets.

foodScene.name: Cafes and the night market in town
foodScene.note: The city center has plenty of new cafes, plus a night market that gathers Isan street food for an evening of grazing.

attractions.name: Pha Taem National Park
attractions.blurb: A cliff above the Mekong with prehistoric rock paintings and a viewpoint over the wide river toward Laos.

attractions.name: Sam Phan Bok
attractions.blurb: Rocky rapids in the middle of the Mekong that surface in the dry season, with thousands of oddly shaped stone basins to explore on foot.

attractions.name: Saeng Chan Waterfall (the Hole Waterfall)
attractions.blurb: A waterfall where the water streams down through a hole in the rock. In the Pha Taem area, best from the rainy season into early winter.

attractions.name: Sao Chaliang
attractions.blurb: Mushroom-shaped stone pillars formed by natural erosion, near Pha Taem — a handy photo stop along the way.

attractions.name: Wat Sirindhorn Wararam Phu Prao
attractions.blurb: A hillside temple with a wishing tree that glows green after dark behind the ordination hall — the highlight people come for.

attractions.name: Wat Thung Si Muang
attractions.blurb: An old temple in the city center with a scripture hall over water and old murals inside the ordination hall.

attractions.name: Thung Si Muang
attractions.blurb: A park in the heart of the city that serves as the ground for the Candle Festival, with the city pillar shrine and seating where locals relax.

attractions.name: Ubon Ratchathani National Museum
attractions.blurb: An old building in the city center displaying artifacts and the history of lower Isan from prehistoric times onward.
